summary: CRT structured-exception filter. Reads the thread-local storage block, searches the exception-handler record table for a matching record keyed by the exception parameter, and returns to the Win32 unhandled-exception filter when no usable record is found. Otherwise dispatches: handler value 5 clears the record slot and returns 1 (treated as handled/terminate), handler value 1 returns -1 (continue search), and any other handler maps the record's structured exception code to a signal number (130/131/132/133/134/138 or 129 for the divide/overflow code family) then invokes the handler with the mapped code. Called by sub_58A19E (0058a19e).

local_names.this: receiver whose identity keys the handler-record search
local_names.a1: first parameter passed through to ArrayOfStructStrideSearch as the lookup key
local_names.ExceptionInfo: Win32 EXCEPTION_POINTERS for the current fault
local_names.v10: previous signal slot value saved across the handler call
local_names.v11: previous TLS+84 value saved across the handler call

operations.description: TLSValueRetrievalWithInit obtains the thread-local storage block for the current thread
ArrayOfStructStrideSearch(a1, TLS[20]) searches the exception-handler record table rooted in the TLS block for a record matching a1
If no matching handler record is found, return UnhandledExceptionFilter(ExceptionInfo) so the Win32 default filter processes the fault
If the handler function pointer at record+8 is null, return UnhandledExceptionFilter(ExceptionInfo)
If handler pointer equals 5, the record is treated as terminated: clear record+8 to 0 and return 1 (handled)
If handler pointer is not 1, save TLS[21] into v11, store ExceptionInfo into TLS[21] for the duration of dispatch, and restore it afterward
Dispatch mode v6 = record+4: when equal to 8 the exception-code-to-signal mapping path runs; otherwise the record slot is cleared and the handler is invoked directly with v6
Zero-fill the handler-state entries from index dword_5E7888 up to dword_5E7888 + dword_5E788C inside the TLS array at TLS[20], each entry 12 bytes wide with the zero written at entry-end minus 4

Map the structured exception code at record+0 to a signal number in TLS[22]: -1073741683 to 130, -1073741682 to 131, -1073741681 to 134, -1073741680 to 129, -1073741679 to 132, -1073741678 to 138, -1073741677 to 133; the previous TLS[22] value v10 is restored after the handler call
Invoke the mapped handler with argument 8, then restore TLS[22] to v10
After dispatch (or when the handler was 1), return -1 to signal the filter chain to continue
This filter is invoked from sub_58A19E (0058a19e)
